sources.entry: tkinter - (Python standard library) The standard Python interface to the Tcl/Tk GUI toolkit.

summary.name: tkinter
summary.one_liner: tkinter is Python's standard-library interface to the Tcl/Tk GUI toolkit, used to build desktop windows and widgets.
use_cases: Building a simple desktop GUI in Python
Creating forms with labels, entries and buttons
Showing file open/save and message dialogs
Drawing turtle graphics in a window
Running IDLE-style editors built on Tk
summary.what_it_does: The tkinter package wraps the Tcl/Tk toolkit so Python programs can create windows, widgets (classic and themed via tkinter.ttk), and dialogs. It builds Tcl command strings and runs them in an embedded Tcl interpreter. The page explains widget hierarchy, configuration options, and three geometry managers (grid, pack, place). It also covers linking widgets to variables such as StringVar, controlling top-level windows through the window manager, and threading rules, including that the event loop must keep running. Supporting modules include filedialog, messagebox, colorchooser, font and scrolledtext.
notable: Ships with CPython as the standard GUI library, so no extra install is needed where it is present
Includes both the classic Tk widgets and the modern themed tkinter.ttk widget set
Running python -m tkinter opens a demo window and shows the installed Tcl/Tk version
caveats: Tkinter is an optional module; it may be missing from some Python builds and must come from the distributor
Classic Tk widgets have a dated appearance; the page recommends ttk for modern styling
Single-threaded Tcl event loop means long computations must be moved to timers or other threads
